name: NBI-1117568
summary: NBI-1117568 (direclidine) is Neurocrine's oral, once-daily, selective M4 muscarinic agonist for schizophrenia, in-licensed from Nxera (formerly Sosei Heptares) in 2021. It needs no peripheral blocker, unlike Cobenfy. The Phase 2 met its primary endpoint at 20 mg once daily: PANSS total at week 6, p=0.011, effect size 0.61 (NBIX FY2024 10-K, 0000914475-25-000037). Four Phase 3 studies are recruiting: two 284-patient inpatient acute studies with a week-5 PANSS primary endpoint, NCT06963034 (primary completion 2027-10) and NCT07105098 (2027-11); relapse prevention NCT07227818 (2029-07); and long-term safety NCT07114874 (2031-12). Neurocrine guides to topline data in 2027. Price anchor: Cobenfy, the only marketed muscarinic, at its published WAC of $1,887 per 30 days ($22,959 a year), less the 44% Vraylar discount CMS published for 2027. Pool: the book's 1,200,448 prevalence, plus a US incidence of 201,931 new schizophrenia diagnoses a year added at second read (Finnerty et al. 2024, MarketScan rate on US adults, a judgement). Uptake anchor: Cobenfy's 2026 new starts, backed out of BMS's filed US sales, are 0.97% a year of that pool plus one year's incidence (1.14% with no inflow). Nxera receives a tiered royalty from high single digit to mid-teens (NBIX 8-K, 2021-11-22), netted at 7%.

therapy_mode.source: Book trials table and context file: NCT07227818 'Efficacy of NBI-1117568 in Preventing Relapse in Adults With Schizophrenia' (primary outcome time from randomisation to relapse) and NCT07114874 'Long-Term Evaluation of NBI-1117568 in Adults With Schizophrenia'; once-daily oral dosing (NBIX FY2024 10-K, 0000914475-25-000037)
therapy_mode.note: A daily oral antipsychotic taken as maintenance, so chronic by the house definition
therapy_mode.check: Book trials table: NCT07227818 primary outcome 'Time From Randomization to Relapse' (start 2025-12-16, primary completion 2029-07, estimated) and NCT07114874 'Long-Term Evaluation', primary outcome treatment-emergent adverse events, n=600. Neurocrine FY2024 10-K (0000914475-25-000037, book filing_sections): Phase 2 'met its primary endpoint for the once-daily 20 mg dose ... PANSS total score at Week 6 (p=0.011 and effect size of 0.61)'. A daily maintenance antipsychotic is chronic

list_price_per_patient.source: Cobenfy WAC $1,887 per 30 days (Bristol Myers Squibb pricing disclosure, bmspricinginformation.com/cobenfy/cobenfy; cobenfy.com FAQs), x 365/30 = $22,959 a year. Launch WAC was $1,850 a month, which BMS put at $22,500 a year (CNBC 2024-09-26; BioPharma Dive; BMS UK pricing statement, bms.com/news-and-media/statements/cobenfy-uk-pricing.html)
list_price_per_patient.note: Judgement: a published list price for the comparator, not for direclidine. The brief ranks a named list price above the CMS convention. Cobenfy is the closest marketed comparator: it is the only muscarinic agonist on the market, it treats the same disease, and its label (schizophrenia in adults, BMY FY2025 10-K 0000014272-26-000004) is the one direclidine's acute inpatient programme would produce. The CMS convention cannot be read for Cobenfy: lookup.py demand Cobenfy shows Part D 2024 at $2,359,550 over 961 beneficiaries, $2,455 each, and that is its launch quarter only (US launch October 2024). Case for lower: BMS said Cobenfy is priced 'in line with existing branded oral schizophrenia treatments' (BioPharma Dive, via search), but Vraylar's 2024 list was $1,376 per 30 days (CMS IPAY 2027 fact sheet), 27% below Cobenfy's current WAC. Its CMS Part D figure is $9,662 per beneficiary in 2024 (lookup.py demand Vraylar), and Caplyta's is $9,940. A second entrant to the class may also price at or below the first. Case for higher: a once-daily pill with no trospium may be positioned at parity or at a premium to a twice-daily one
list_price_per_patient.check: WAC $1,887 per 30 days on bmspricinginformation.com/cobenfy/cobenfy (search, 2026-09-24). 1,887 x 365/30 = $22,958.50 = 0.0229585, stored 0.022959. Launch: a BMS spokesperson put the list at $22,500 a year, 'in line with the landscape of branded oral antipsychotics' (search; $22,500 x 30/365 = $1,849 per 30 days, consistent with the $1,850 launch WAC the researcher uses for 2024-2025). ANCHOR TEST against CMS: Cobenfy Part D 2024 (lookup.py demand Cobenfy) $2,359,550 over 75,858 dosage units = $31.10 a capsule; at the label's one capsule twice a day (EMERGENT-2, Kaul et al., Lancet 2024, PMID 38104575: dosed twice per day) that is $1,866 per 30 days, within 1% of the $1,850 WAC, so CMS gross spend runs at WAC and WAC is the right list basis. $2,455 per beneficiary over 961 in 2024 is launch-quarter only: BMY FY2025 10-K (book filing_sections) 'approved by the FDA in September 2024 and launched in the U.S. in October 2024', label 'treatment of schizophrenia in adults'. Comparators reproduced: Vraylar list $1,376 per 30 days (CMS IPAY 2027 fact sheet, search), 27.1% below $1,887; Vraylar Part D 2024 $9,662 and Caplyta $9,940 per beneficiary (lookup.py demand). Judgement labelled, cases for and against stated, inputs confirmed

gross_to_net_pct.source: CMS, Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program, negotiated prices for initial price applicability year 2027 (cms.gov/files/document/fact-sheet-negotiated-prices-ipay-2027.pdf): Vraylar list price $1,376 per 30-day supply (2024), negotiated price $770, a 44% discount. The $770 is in the book (negotiated_prices, VRAYLAR, mfp_30des 770, effective 2027-01-01, source cms_mfp). 1 - 770/1,376 = 0.4404
gross_to_net_pct.note: Judgement. A WAC anchor takes neither house convention, so the discount must be sourced, and this is the only published list-to-net discount found for a branded oral antipsychotic in schizophrenia. Direction checked: 44.04% comes off list, so net is $12,848 per patient-year. Case for a smaller discount: CMS negotiated the price for a drug a decade past launch, and gross_to_net.py calls such a price conservative for a fresh launch. Antipsychotics are also a protected Part D class with thin rebates. Case for a larger discount: BMS puts more than 80% of schizophrenia patients on Medicare or Medicaid (BioPharma Dive, via search). Medicaid takes a statutory 23.1% basic rebate plus supplemental and inflation rebates, and from 2025 Part D adds a 10% to 20% manufacturer discount. The book's other WAC discount, 0.2777 from Kalydeco, is not used: its own row calls it a floor that mostly measures fill coverage, and it comes from cystic fibrosis
gross_to_net_pct.check: CMS fact sheet, negotiated prices IPAY 2027 (search): Vraylar list $1,376, negotiated $770, a 44% discount, effective 2027-01-01. Book negotiated_prices: VRAYLAR, ipay 2027, mfp_30des 770 on eight NDC rows, cms_mfp. 1 - 770/1,376 = 0.440407. Direction right: share OFF list, net = 0.5596 x $22,958.5 = $12,847 per patient-year. A WAC anchor takes a sourced discount (brief), and this one is sourced. TEST OF THE WAC ANCHOR WITH THIS DISCOUNT: penetration_peak_pct is solved from Cobenfy's net sales divided by this same net price, so the discount moves price and patients in opposite directions and largely cancels. Engine run (forecast.derive_new_patients and treated_stock, start 2030, k 1.065, midpoint 2.01, stop 0.5936, no incidence): at 0.4404 the solved peak is 1.1387%, the stock tops out at 21,551 and revenue at $277mm; at the Part D 0.5 it is 1.2760%, 23,990 and $275mm; at Kalydeco's 0.2777 it is 0.8801%, 16,865 and $280mm. Peak revenue moves under 2% across the range, so the anchor passes. It stays a judgement: the $770 is a statutory Medicare ceiling on a 2015 launch, not a commercial gross-to-net. The researcher's '>80% of schizophrenia patients on Medicare or Medicaid' was not cleanly confirmed by search; it sits only in the case for a larger discount and feeds no value

discontinuation_pct.unit: share of treated stock stopping per year
discontinuation_pct.source: CATIE (Lieberman JA et al., N Engl J Med 2005;353:1209-1223, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa051688, PMID 16172203): 1,061 of 1,432 US patients with chronic schizophrenia (74%) stopped their oral antipsychotic within 18 months
discontinuation_pct.note: Constant hazard: 1 - (1 - 1061/1432)^(12/18) = 0.5936 a year. This is the class's reference measure of all-cause discontinuation, in the label's population, on oral daily antipsychotics. Case for higher: the muscarinic class so far keeps fewer patients. In EMERGENT-4, 34 of the 156 who enrolled in the 52-week xanomeline-trospium extension completed it, 21.8%, so 78.2% stopped (Kaul I et al., Am J Psychiatry 2026;183(3):183-192, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.20241186, PMID 41634905). Case for lower: EMERGENT-5 reported 51% withdrawal over 52 weeks (a secondary figure, from the review by Ji F et al., Ther Adv Psychopharmacol 2026, doi:10.1177/20451253261478086, PMID 42621264). Direclidine avoids trospium and the twice-daily schedule, which may improve persistence. The same rate is used to back out Cobenfy's new starts in penetration_peak_pct, so the two stay consistent
discontinuation_pct.check: CATIE abstract (PubMed 16172203, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa051688): 57 US sites; 'Overall, 74 percent of patients discontinued the study medication before 18 months (1061 of the 1432 patients who received at least one dose)'. 1 - (371/1,432)^(12/18) = 0.593600. Case for higher confirmed: EMERGENT-4 abstract (PMID 41634905) 156 of 366 enrolled, '34 (21.8%) enrolled participants completed the 52-week treatment period', so 78.2% stopped. Case for lower confirmed: Ji et al. 2026 review abstract (PMID 42621264): 'EMERGENT-4: 78.2% discontinuation; EMERGENT-5: 51% withdrawal'. The same 0.5936 is used in the penetration back-out, as stated

forecast_start_year.source: Primary completion NCT06963034 2027-10 and NCT07105098 2027-11, both estimated (book trials table). Neurocrine expects 'initial topline data ... in 2027' (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007) and 'Phase 3 readouts for ... direclidine in schizophrenia' in 2027 (Q2 2026 results, 8-K 0000914475-26-000035). Precedent: Karuna submitted the KarXT NDA in September 2023 and the FDA approved Cobenfy on 26 September 2024, a standard 12-month review (Karuna NDA acceptance release, 2023-11-29, via search; BMY FY2024 10-K 0000014272-25-000039). That approval rested on acute placebo-controlled trials plus open-label safety data of up to one year (BMY FY2024 10-K)
forecast_start_year.note: Judgement on the timeline. Topline around the turn of 2028, an NDA about six months later, and a standard review put approval around mid-2029, so 2030 is the first full year. Neither the relapse-prevention study (2029-07) nor the long-term study (2031-12) should gate the filing, since Cobenfy was approved without a relapse-prevention study. The long-term study began in July 2025, so one-year exposures exist by 2028. Case for 2029: the book's usual rule, the second calendar year after primary completion, gives 2029, and a filing early in 2028 would leave most of 2029 on market. Case for 2031: a failure in one acute study would mean running another.
forecast_start_year.check: Book trials table: NCT06963034 primary completion 2027-10 (estimated, start 2025-05-08), NCT07105098 2027-11 (estimated, start 2025-08-11), NCT07227818 2029-07, NCT07114874 2031-12 (start 2025-07-11). FY2025 10-K (0000914475-26-000007, filing_sections): 'with initial topline data expected in 2027'. Q2 2026 results exhibit (8-K 0000914475-26-000035): 'multiple important clinical milestones in 2027, including Phase 3 readouts for osavampator ... and direclidine in schizophrenia'. Karuna submitted the KarXT NDA in September 2023 with a PDUFA date of 26 September 2024 (search: BioSpace, Fierce Biotech, Karuna 8-K), and BMY's FY2025 10-K confirms FDA approval in September 2024. EMERGENT-4 was the 52-week open-label extension (PMID 41634905), consistent with approval on acute trials plus open-label safety. Topline around end-2027, NDA mid-2028, standard review to mid-2029: 2030 as first full year holds, and matches the sibling NBI-1065845 (verified 2030). Judgement labelled with both cases

exus_multiple.source: No filed split supports an ex-US product line. Neurocrine: 'We sell INGREZZA exclusively in the U.S.', and valbenazine abroad is sold by Tanabe Pharma, which retains the rights there (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007). Cobenfy, the class comparator: FY2025 US $155mm, Non-US nil (BMY FY2025 10-K 0000014272-26-000004, in the book's asset_revenue_regions)
exus_multiple.note: Left null, and the engine reads null as nil. Neurocrine holds global rights to direclidine (FY2025 10-K) but has never sold a product outside the US, and its pattern is to license ex-US rights for a royalty, which this field cannot express. Case for a value: J&J's schizophrenia-only paliperidone franchise (Invega Sustenna/Xeplion/Trinza/Trevicta) booked $1,085mm outside the US against $2,725mm in the US in FY2025, 0.398 (book asset_revenue_regions, 10-K 0000200406-26-000016). That is a large-cap company with a global sales force. Vraylar reads 0.0025 ($9mm against $3,612mm, AbbVie 0001551152-26-000008) because Gedeon Richter holds Vraylar's ex-US rights
exus_multiple.check: Null confirmed. FY2025 10-K (filing_sections): 'We sell INGREZZA exclusively in the U.S.'; Tanabe Pharma 'retains commercialization rights' to valbenazine in Japan and select Asian markets; 'Direclidine was in-licensed from Nxera ... and we retain global rights'. The FY2024 10-K said 'excluding in Japan'; the 2026 10-Qs resolve it: Nxera retains Japan only for 'compounds comprised of M1 receptor agonists'. Book asset_revenue_regions FY2025: Cobenfy US $155mm, Non-US 0; paliperidone franchise $1,085mm / $2,725mm = 0.398; Vraylar $9mm / $3,612mm = 0.0025

economics_share.source: Neurocrine 8-K of 2021-11-22 (0000914475-21-000062, EX-99.1, sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/914475/000091447521000062/nbix-20211122exhibit991.htm): Sosei Heptares, now Nxera, receives $100mm upfront and development, regulatory and commercial milestones, and is 'eligible to receive tiered royalties ranging from high single digit to mid-teen percentage on future net sales'. Q2 2026 10-Q (0000914475-26-000037, note 10) and Q1 2026 10-Q (0000914475-26-000026): Nxera 'is entitled to receive royalties on the future net sales of any collaboration product' and up to $2.48bn in further milestones. Neurocrine bears all development, manufacturing and commercialisation costs. Royalties run to the latest of last patent expiry, a set number of years from first sale, and regulatory exclusivity. FY2025 10-K (0000914475-26-000007): 'Direclidine was in-licensed from Nxera ... in 2021, and we retain global rights.' Nxera's retained Japan rights cover M1 agonists only (10-Q), and direclidine is M4-selective. Margin: Neurocrine has no company rows in the book, so it is taken from the FY2025 filed lines in the book's financials table (edgar_companyfacts), the method block.py uses. Revenue $2,860.5mm; cost of revenue $52.1mm (0.018214); SG&A $1,156.2mm (0.404195); R&D $1,015.7mm (0.355078); other_costs_pct not yet derived, taken as 0. Margin = 0.222514. (0.222514 - 0.07) / 0.222514 = 0.685412
economics_share.note: A royalty Neurocrine PAYS, netted as (margin - royalty) / margin, the book's convention. Judgement on the tier: 'high single digit' is taken at its bottom, 7%, exactly as the disitamab vedotin seed nets the same filed wording. Provisional on the margin: re-strike this once Neurocrine's company rows land. A positive other_costs_pct lowers the share; at a margin of 0.20 it would be 0.65. Case lower: a 12% blended royalty gives 0.4607, and the 15% top tier 0.3259. Case higher: Neurocrine's R&D is 35.5% of revenue, and netting against a margin that low makes a 7% royalty cost 31% of the asset. Milestones (up to $2.48bn across all collaboration products) are not netted, as in the book's other royalty seeds. The $35mm Phase 2 milestone and $15mm Phase 3 start milestone are already paid (FY2024 10-K; Q2 2026 10-Q)
economics_share.check: ROYALTY WORDING: search surfaced the Neurocrine and Sosei Heptares release of 22 November 2021 and its filing as EX-99.1 to 8-K 0000914475-21-000062 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/914475/000091447521000062/nbix-20211122exhibit991.htm): US$100mm upfront and 'tiered royalties ranging from high single digit to mid-teen percentage on future net sales'. The book's filing_sections does not hold that 8-K (its NBIX filings start 2022-08-04 and its sections 2025-02-10), so the wording is confirmed by search, not read from the exhibit in the book. What the book's filings confirm (10-Q 0000914475-26-000026 note 7; 10-Q 0000914475-26-000037 note 10): Nxera 'is entitled to receive royalties on the future net sales of any collaboration product' and 'up to $2.48 billion' of event-based milestones; 'We are responsible for all development, manufacturing, and commercialization costs'; the royalty term runs to the later of last patent expiry, a number of years from first sale, and regulatory exclusivity; Nxera's Japan rights cover M1 agonist compounds only. Milestones paid: $35mm on Phase 2 (FY2024 10-K MD&A) and $15mm on the May 2025 Phase 3 start, expensed Q2 2025 (Q2 2026 10-Q). ROYALTY SHARE OF SALES CONFIRMED: 0.07, the bottom of 'high single digit', the reading the disitamab vedotin seed makes of the identical wording (lookup.py seed Disitamab: (0.229497 - 0.07) / 0.229497 = 0.6950). Re-strike on Neurocrine's final cost block as (margin - 0.07) / margin. Margin recomputed from book financials, NBIX FY2025 FY, edgar_companyfacts: revenue $2,860.5mm, CostOfRevenue $52.1mm (0.018214), SG&A $1,156.2mm (0.404195), R&D $1,015.7mm (0.355078), margin 0.222514 with other_costs 0; (0.222514 - 0.07) / 0.222514 = 0.685412. Sensitivities reproduced: 12% 0.4607, 15% 0.3259, margin 0.20 gives 0.65. Cautions for the re-strike: the share reaches zero at other_costs_pct 0.1525; filed operating income was $619.1mm (0.2164), so $17.4mm of cost sits outside the three lines (0.6766 on that margin); the May 2026 Soleno acquisition ($23.1mm of acquisition expense in the Q2 2026 10-Q) changes the cost base the final block will carry. Milestones are outside the field, as the note says

prevalence.source: carried by the book (epidemiology.csv: 1,200,448, NIMH midpoint of 0.25%-0.64% for schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders, applied to US adults)
prevalence.note: Carried by the book. The file calls it its softest row: 674,409 at the low end and 1,726,486 at the high end. It is broader than the label, because it includes related psychotic disorders
prevalence.check: lookup.py pool Schizophrenia: epidemiology.csv 1,200,448 (NIMH 0.25%-0.64% midpoint on US adults), low 674,409, high 1,726,486; no asset rows. Null is right. assumptions.py fills prevalence and incidence one field at a time (only where the asset's own value is None), so the book's prevalence still fills this asset alongside the incidence set below

incidence.source: Finnerty et al., 'Prevalence and incidence measures for schizophrenia among commercial health insurance and medicaid enrollees', npj Schizophrenia 2024;10:68, doi:10.1038/s41537-024-00490-0, PMID 39174558, PMC11341906 (read in full). In IBM MarketScan, 712 of 951,173 people continuously insured from 2009 to 2019 had a new diagnosis of schizophrenia in 2019, 0.07% (95% CI 0.07-0.08): two or more claims for schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder (ICD-10 F20, F25; schizophreniform excluded) in 2019 and no schizophrenia diagnosis in the prior ten years, a look-back the paper validates as its reference standard. Applied to the adult base the book's prevalence row implies (1,200,448 / 0.445% = 269,763,596): 269,763,596 x 712/951,173 = 201,931
incidence.note: Judgement: a commercially insured rate applied to all US adults. POPULATION IT COUNTS: new claims diagnoses of schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder among employer-insured people of every age with ten years of unbroken coverage and at least one service a year. It is diagnosed incidence, not onset, and narrower in diagnosis than the book's prevalence, which includes related psychotic disorders. Case for higher: in the same study NYS Medicaid ran 1,489 of 785,088 (0.19%), 511,634 a year on this base, and people with schizophrenia are concentrated in Medicaid. Case for lower: 201,931 is 16.8% of the carried prevalence, about six years of diagnosed illness for a lifelong disease, so some 'new' F20/F25 diagnoses are people the NIMH figure already counts under related psychotic disorders; the paper's schizophrenia-only rate (75 per 100,000) is above the chart-confirmed first-episode psychosis rate for ages 30-59 in five US health systems (46 per 100,000, Simon et al., Psychiatr Serv 2017, PMID 28045349, PMC5811263), which counts every psychosis. Cross-check: Teixeira et al. (PLoS One 2022, PMID 36137136) found 1.04 per 1,000 Optum adults newly diagnosed with schizophrenia disorders in 2020; Finnerty's MarketScan PPV of 81% at a one-year look-back takes that to about 0.84 per 1,000, near this 0.75. ENGINE WARNING: forecast.derive_new_patients adds incidence x eligible_pct to the untreated pool every year with no deaths. At this inflow and the re-solved peak the untreated pool passes the NIMH high end (1,726,486) in 2032 and reaches 3.88mm by 2044, and revenue climbs without a plateau to about $801mm in 2044. An untreated_carryover_pct of prevalence / (prevalence + incidence) = 0.8560 holds the pool at the carried prevalence (stock tops out near 22,100, about $284mm); it is not set here because no source states it. Carry this figure in epidemiology.csv rather than on this asset alone, so no second schizophrenia asset carries a different one
incidence.check: Researcher left it null and rejected Teixeira 2022 as counting prevalent patients newly seen in claims. A ten-year washout answers that objection for schizophrenia codes, and the caller asked for a study-based US incidence of diagnosed schizophrenia if one could be sourced. Finnerty et al. 2024 read in full via PubMed Central: MarketScan 10-year continuously insured cohort 951,173, incident 712 (0.07%), prevalence 0.159%; NYS Medicaid cohort 785,088, incident 1,489 (0.19%), prevalence 5.74%; incidence required two or more F20/F25 claims in 2019 and none in 2009-2018. 712/951,173 = 0.00074855; x 269,763,596 = 201,931. Other US candidates read and not used: Simon et al. 2017 (PMC5811263, full text) counts any first psychosis, including mood and substance-related, ages 15-59, 86 and 46 per 100,000; Chung et al., Am J Psychiatry 2023 (PMID 37789743, Kaiser Permanente Northern California, 5,994,758 members) gives no overall rate in its abstract and its full text was not reachable (Amass quota exhausted); Pilon et al. 2021 (PMID 34281472) is Medicaid-only (0.31%-0.39% a year); Breitborde et al. 2026 (PMID 41535736) is first-episode psychosis at ages 15-40 (80.54 per 100,000). Engine runs (forecast.py functions, 2030 start, 15 years) behind the warning in the note: no incidence and peak 0.0114, stock tops out at 21,574, $277mm; incidence 201,931 and peak 0.009732, stock 62,312 and $801mm in 2044, still rising; the same with carryover 0.8560, stock 22,132, $284mm

eligible_pct.source: Label basis: Cobenfy is 'indicated for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults' (BMY FY2025 10-K 0000014272-26-000004), approved on EMERGENT-2/-3. Those trials enrolled adults aged 18-65 recently hospitalised for worsening psychosis, with PANSS of 80 or more and CGI-S of 4 or more (EMERGENT-2, Kaul I et al., Lancet 2024;403:160-170, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(23)02190-6, PMID 38104575). Direclidine's Phase 3 acute studies use the same acute inpatient design (NCT06963034, NCT07105098: 'Inpatient Adults With Schizophrenia', PANSS at week 5)
eligible_pct.note: Judgement. In schizophrenia the Phase 3 entry criteria (acute exacerbation, inpatient, PANSS 80 or more) do not carry into the label: the same design gave Cobenfy an all-adults label. The drug has no biomarker, and no line of therapy is stated. The book's pool is already adults. No filter is applied, for two reasons. The pool's excess over the label (related psychotic disorders, and the untreated) has no sourced share. And penetration_peak_pct is solved from Cobenfy on this same 1.0 basis, so any filter here would scale the solved peak up by the same factor and leave patients almost unchanged. Case for a filter: the label reaches schizophrenia only, and a patient outside care cannot be started
eligible_pct.check: Cobenfy label 'treatment of schizophrenia in adults' (BMY FY2025 10-K, book filing_sections). EMERGENT-2 abstract (PMID 38104575): adults 18-65 'with a recent worsening of psychosis warranting hospital admission', PANSS 80 or more, CGI-S 4 or more, 22 US inpatient sites. NCT06963034 and NCT07105098 (book trials): 'Inpatient Adults With Schizophrenia', primary outcome PANSS total at week 5. The cancellation argument holds with the incidence now set too: a filter would scale both the pool and the inflow, and the re-solved peak up by the same factor. Judgement labelled, case for a filter stated

penetration_peak_pct.unit: share of the untreated eligible pool per year
penetration_peak_pct.source: Cobenfy, measured from BMS's filed US net sales: $10mm in FY2024 (launch October 2024), $155mm in FY2025 (10-K 0000014272-26-000004, all US) and $119mm in H1 2026 ($56mm in Q1, $63mm in Q2; 8-Ks 0000014272-26-000008 and -000018; book asset_revenue). Each is divided by the net price on the same basis as this seed: WAC ($1,850 per 30 days in 2024-2025, $1,887 in 2026) x 365/30 x (1 - 0.4404). That gives patient-years on therapy of 794 (2024), 12,306 (2025) and 18,525 (2026, H1 annualised). The engine's stock recursion at the 0.5936 stop rate backs out new starts of 11,983 in 2025 and 13,524 in 2026. The engine's eligible pool in a year is the untreated pool plus that year's incidence, so the 2026 capture is 13,524 over the book's pool less the patients already started (1,200,448 - 794 - 11,983 = 1,187,671) plus one year of the incidence set above (201,931): 13,524 / 1,389,603 = 0.9732%
penetration_peak_pct.note: Judgement: 1.0x Cobenfy's second-full-year capture, used as the peak, re-solved at second read for the incidence added above (1.1387% on the same data with no inflow; use that figure if the incidence is not adopted). Cobenfy's new starts rose only 13% from 2025 to 2026 (11,983 to 13,524) while its revenue grew on the carried stock, so its capture looks near a plateau rather than early on a ramp. Case for higher: Cobenfy is still growing (Q2 2026 annualised gives 1.05% with the incidence); a 0.78 stop rate (EMERGENT-4) gives 1.14%, and a 0.5 discount 1.09%. The consensus peak the book carries for Cobenfy, $3.9bn (revenue_ceiling_musd), would need about 303,600 patient-years, new starts of some 15% of the prevalence a year. Neurocrine sells Ingrezza to the same psychiatrists, and a once-daily M4 agonist without trospium may tolerate better. Case for lower: direclidine is second into a class that BMS is still struggling to move past 'deeply ingrained D2 prescribing habits' (BMS Q3 2025 results, 8-K 0000014272-25-000147). Cobenfy's adjunctive ARISE study missed (BMY FY2025 10-K). Cobenfy's 2025 starts include a launch bolus of waiting switchers. The Kalydeco 0.2777 discount would give 0.75%. With the incidence and no exit from the pool the engine's stock does not settle: see the incidence note

untreated_carryover_pct.unit: share of the untreated pool retained per year
untreated_carryover_pct.source: derived to hold the schizophrenia pool at its measured size, the method the remternetug seed uses: the book's prevalence (epidemiology.csv, NIMH, 1,200,448 x eligible_pct 1.0) and its inflow (201,931 a year, Finnerty 2024) are stationary only if exits equal entries, which sets retention at 1,200,448 / (1,200,448 + 201,931) = 0.8560
untreated_carryover_pct.note: JUDGEMENT. The engine models no exit from the untreated pool (deaths, remission, loss to care), so at full carryover the second reader measured it passing NIMH's high-end prevalence by 2032 and revenue still rising in 2044. Holding it stationary is the book's answer to the same problem on remternetug. The case against: diagnosed schizophrenia is lifelong for most, so the true exit rate is mortality (standardised mortality about 2.5 times the population's), lower than 14% a year, and the stationary pool understates a growing diagnosed population
